scope: Prayer text completeness and recording/text version distinction. New translations and instructions are editorial summaries; traditional Arabic prayer texts retain their source variants.

checks.result: Added Arabic, transliteration and meanings for both inneke la tuhliful-miad and wad-darajatar-rafiah. Diyanet identifies the ending as an addition in some narrations (Beyhaki); the MEB teaching sheet publishes this extended wording. Critically, Portal HTML omits clauses that the actual existing MP3 DOES recite: the audio audit in test-results/dua-asr-review.json finds wad-darajatar-rafiah at about 15-18s and the ending at about 23-28s. No short-version warning is assigned, and the matched extended text accompanies the existing audio unchanged.

Existing Arabic omitted ve celle senauk while transliteration inserted it in parentheses. The prayer-practice catalog now keeps the ordinary-prayer transliteration consistent with its Arabic, and separately explains the funeral-prayer addition. Original NAMAZ array is preserved.

Existing Arabic prayer wording compared with the Portal HTML. No missing terminal prayer clause identified. Kunut 1 and 2 and both Rabbena prayers remain paired as in their source recordings; no unrelated audio or inferred word timings assigned.

Compared with rendered page 70, including the full neveytu intention and the closing praise. Existing long text is complete; it remains identified as a traditional pre-recitation supplication, not an obligatory formula. Native audio availability remains a separate audit.

Existing short thanksgiving is retained and explicitly titled short. A separate long version from visually checked pages 112-113 includes blessings for the host, provision, health, pardon, prayer, parents, believers and closing praise. The source's final al-Fatiha reading direction is instructional guidance rather than inserted as a spoken Arabic prayer clause. The collective long example is not claimed to be one indivisible obligatory prophetic formula.

Arabic uses the aqibati amri wording in both good/bad branches; narrator alternatives (aw qala) are not inserted into the prayer. Includes transliteration, Turkish/English meaning, research and consultation, two voluntary rakahs (Fatihah+Kafirun then Fatihah+Ikhlas), subsequent dua, no required dream or colour divination, and dua alone when prayer cannot be performed. No invented success guarantee, posture, silence rule or compulsory bedtime is prescribed.

Short bedtime and waking prayers added with Arabic, transliteration and Turkish/English meanings. Bedtime uses the source's bismike ahya wa bismike amut variant; it is not silently mixed with another wording.
Adds the short mounting prayer from Quran 43:13-14. Explicitly distinguishes this from longer travel supplications and explains the preceding three takbirs.
Uses the short leke sumtu wa ala rizqika aftartu wording published by Diyanet. Longer variants exist; absence of extra phrases in this short version is not labelled a defect.
Quran 20:114 prayer Rabbi zidni ilma, already present in the Quran-prayers tab, is exposed in this learning catalog as well. Quran reference preserved; no new unrelated recording assigned.

audioPolicy: This content audit adds no recording to an item merely because its text is known. Added native recordings require an independent identity, content and use-basis audit. Existing seven manifest entries were not edited here.
regressionChecks: tests/dua-content.test.mjs: extended ezan ending and lofty-rank clause matching the actual recording; separate short/long meal versions; complete Quran-opening intention; both istikhara branches and practical guidance; source/meaning availability; ordinary Subhaneke pronunciation consistency.
